questions.subtopic: Three Key Von Neumann Concepts
questions.concept: Three key concepts of the Von Neumann architecture
questions.question: Which of the following accurately states the three key concepts of the Von Neumann architecture developed at the Institute for Advanced Studies, Princeton?
options: (1) Data and instructions are stored in a single read-write memory; (2) Memory contents are addressable by location without regard to data type; (3) Execution occurs sequentially from one instruction to the next unless explicitly modified
(1) Instructions and data are stored in separate memories; (2) Memory is addressed by variable name; (3) All instructions execute simultaneously in parallel
(1) Programs are hardwired by connecting physical logic gates; (2) Only decimal numbers are stored; (3) Interrupts are prohibited
(1) Cache replaces main memory; (2) All I/O uses DMA exclusively; (3) Control units are strictly hardwired
questions.explanationEn: Slide 3 (p. 2) lists the three key concepts of the von Neumann architecture: (1) Data and instructions are stored in a single read-write memory; (2) Memory contents are addressable by location without regard to the type of data contained there; (3) Execution occurs in a sequential fashion (unless explicitly modified) from one instruction to the next.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 3 (trang 2) nêu 3 nguyên lý cốt lõi của kiến trúc von Neumann: (1) Dữ liệu và lệnh được lưu chung trong một bộ nhớ đọc-ghi duy nhất; (2) Nội dung bộ nhớ được định địa chỉ theo vị trí không phụ thuộc kiểu dữ liệu; (3) Việc thực thi diễn ra tuần tự từ lệnh này sang lệnh kế tiếp trừ khi bị thay đổi tường minh.

questions.subtopic: Hardwired vs. Software Programs
questions.concept: Hardwired program definition
questions.question: In the context of computer components (Slide 3), what is meant by a 'hardwired program'?
options: A high-level C++ program compiled with static linking
The result of physically connecting the various hardware logic components in the desired configuration to perform a specific computation
An operating system kernel stored in a solid-state drive
A sequence of machine instructions fetched dynamically from RAM via the system bus
questions.explanationEn: Slide 3 defines a hardwired program as 'the result of the process of connecting the various components in the desired configuration.' Unlike software programs, changing the task requires rewiring the hardware.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 3 định nghĩa 'hardwired program' (chương trình kết dây cứng) là kết quả của việc kết nối trực tiếp các thành phần phần cứng theo cấu hình mong muốn.

questions.subtopic: PC, IR, MAR, MBR & I/O Registers
questions.concept: Roles of PC, IR, MAR, and MBR
questions.question: Which pair of CPU registers interfaces directly with the system bus's Address lines and Data lines, respectively?
options: Program Counter (PC) connects to the Data lines, and Instruction Register (IR) connects to the Address lines
Memory Address Register (MAR) connects to the Address lines, and Memory Buffer Register (MBR) connects to the Data lines
Instruction Register (IR) connects to the Control lines, and Accumulator (AC) connects to the Address lines
Program Status Word (PSW) connects to the Address lines, and Stack Pointer connects to the Data lines
questions.explanationEn: Slide 7 (p. 3) states: 'Memory Address Register (MAR) – usually connected directly to address lines of bus; Memory Buffer Register (MBR) – usually connected directly to data lines of bus.'
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 7 (trang 3): Thanh ghi địa chỉ bộ nhớ (MAR) kết nối trực tiếp với các đường địa chỉ (Address lines) của bus, còn Thanh ghi đệm bộ nhớ (MBR) kết nối trực tiếp với các đường dữ liệu (Data lines) của bus.

questions.subtopic: Program Status Word (PSW) & Optional Registers
questions.concept: Program Status Word (PSW) common flags
questions.question: Which of the following is a flag or field commonly contained in the Program Status Word (PSW) that indicates whether privileged operating-system instructions may be executed?
options: Supervisor flag
Overflow flag
Carry flag
Equal flag
questions.explanationEn: Slide 8 (p. 4) lists the common fields/flags in the PSW: Sign, Zero, Carry, Equal, Overflow, Interrupt Enable/Disable, and Supervisor ('indicates if privileged ops can be used').
questions.explanationVi: Slide 8 (trang 4) liệt kê các cờ trong PSW gồm: Sign, Zero, Carry, Equal, Overflow, Interrupt Enable/Disable, và Supervisor (cho biết có được phép thực thi các lệnh đặc quyền hay không).

questions.subtopic: PC, IR, MAR, MBR & I/O Registers
questions.concept: Sequence of register micro-operations during Instruction Fetch
questions.question: During the instruction fetch cycle illustrated on Slides 12–13, what is the correct chronological order of register and bus operations to fetch the next instruction from memory?
options: 1) IR moves address to MBR -> 2) ALU issues Memory Write -> 3) MAR copies data to PC -> 4) PC is cleared to zero
1) Control Unit increments IR -> 2) Data Bus transfers address to PC -> 3) MAR decodes instruction -> 4) MBR increments PC
1) Memory pushes instruction directly into AC -> 2) AC copies opcode to MAR -> 3) PC reads from Control Bus -> 4) IR writes back to RAM

1) PC address is moved to MAR and placed on Address Bus -> 2) Control Unit issues Memory Read on Control Bus -> 3) Memory places instruction on Data Bus into MBR -> 4) MBR transfers instruction to IR while PC is incremented
questions.explanationEn: Slides 12–13 detail the 7-step diagram: (1) PC contains address of next instruction and moves it to MAR; (2) Address is placed on Address Bus; (3) Control unit requests a memory read via Control Bus; (4–5) Result is placed on Data Bus and copied to MBR; (6) Result is moved from MBR to IR; (7) Meanwhile, PC is incremented.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 12–13 (trang 6): Địa chỉ lệnh kế tiếp từ PC được chuyển sang MAR và đưa lên Address Bus -> Control Unit phát tín hiệu đọc bộ nhớ trên Control Bus -> Kết quả được đưa lên Data Bus vào MBR -> Chuyển từ MBR vào IR, đồng thời PC tự động tăng lên.

questions.subtopic: Hexadecimal Program Execution Trace (Fig 3.5)
questions.concept: Tracing Figure 3.5 Hexadecimal Program Execution
questions.question: In Figure 3.5 (Example of Program Execution, Slide 17), memory contains hexadecimal instructions `300: 1940` (Load AC from memory 940), `301: 5941` (Add to AC from memory 941), and `302: 2941` (Store AC to memory 941), while data memory contains `940: 0003` and `941: 0002`. Starting with `PC = 300`, what are the hexadecimal values of `PC`, `AC`, `IR`, and memory location `941` at the completion of Step 6?
questions.explanationEn: Tracing Figure 3.5 (p. 7): Step 1 fetches `1940` from 300 (`IR=1940`). Step 2 loads `Memory[940]=0003` into `AC` (`AC=0003, PC=301`). Step 3 fetches `5941` from 301 (`IR=5941`). Step 4 adds `Memory[941]=0002` to `AC` (`AC=0003+0002=0005, PC=302`). Step 5 fetches `2941` from 302 (`IR=2941`). Step 6 stores `AC=0005` into `Memory[941]` (`Memory[941]=0005, PC=303, AC=0005, IR=2941`).
questions.explanationVi: Theo Hình 3.5 (trang 7): Bước 1–2 nạp lệnh `1940` tại địa chỉ 300, đưa giá trị ô nhớ `940` (`0003`) vào `AC`. Bước 3–4 nạp lệnh `5941` tại 301, cộng giá trị ô nhớ `941` (`0002`) vào `AC` => `AC = 0005`. Bước 5–6 nạp lệnh `2941` tại 302 (`PC` tăng lên `303`, `IR = 2941`), lưu `AC` (`0005`) vào ô nhớ `941` => `Memory[941] = 0005`.
questions.formula: Opcode 1 = Load AC; Opcode 5 = Add to AC; Opcode 2 = Store AC
questions.stepByStep:
1. Step 1-2 (Addr 300, IR=1940): Load AC <- Mem[940] = 0003; PC becomes 301.
2. Step 3-4 (Addr 301, IR=5941): Add AC <- AC + Mem[941] = 0003 + 0002 = 0005; PC becomes 302.
3. Step 5-6 (Addr 302, IR=2941): Store Mem[941] <- AC = 0005; PC becomes 303.

questions.subtopic: Instruction Cycle State Diagram
questions.concept: Instruction Cycle State Diagram (Figure 3.6)
questions.question: In the Instruction Cycle State Diagram (Figure 3.6, Slide 20), which states have a loop indicating they may be repeated multiple times for a single instruction?
options: Instruction fetch and Instruction address calculation only
Instruction operation decoding only
Halt state and Reset state
Operand fetch (for multiple operands) and Operand store (for multiple results), as well as returning from Operand store to Operand fetch for string or vector data
questions.explanationEn: Figure 3.6 (p. 8) shows self-transitions between Operand Address Calculation and Operand Fetch ('Multiple operands'), between Operand Address Calculation and Operand Store ('Multiple results'), and a loop from Operand Store back to Operand Address Calculation ('Return for string or vector data').
questions.explanationVi: Hình 3.6 (trang 8) chỉ ra các vòng lặp khi lệnh có nhiều toán hạng (Multiple operands giữa tính địa chỉ toán hạng và nạp toán hạng), nhiều kết quả (Multiple results), hoặc xử lý dữ liệu chuỗi/vector (Return for string or vector data).

questions.subtopic: Classes of Interrupts & Software Interrupts
questions.concept: Four classes of hardware/system interrupts
questions.question: According to Table/Slide 22 ('Classes of Interrupts'), into which class of interrupt do 'arithmetic overflow', 'division by zero', and 'attempt to execute an illegal machine instruction' fall?
options: Timer interrupt
Program interrupt
I/O interrupt
Hardware Failure interrupt
questions.explanationEn: Slide 22 classifies interrupts into four categories: Program (arithmetic overflow, division by zero, illegal instruction, memory protection violation), Timer (internal processor timer for OS scheduling), I/O (from I/O controller), and Hardware Failure (power failure, memory parity error).
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 22 (trang 9), các sự kiện như tràn số học (arithmetic overflow), chia cho 0 (division by zero), thực thi lệnh máy không hợp lệ thuộc lớp Ngắt chương trình (Program interrupt).

questions.subtopic: Classes of Interrupts & Software Interrupts
questions.concept: Software Interrupts (INT instruction)
questions.question: Why does Slide 23 state that 'Software interrupts are not really interrupts at all', and what are they typically used for in Intel x86 and ARM processors?
options: Because software interrupts physically disconnect the power supply to the CPU
Because software interrupts are generated randomly by defective RAM chips
Because software interrupts bypass the operating system and overwrite the BIOS ROM

Because a software interrupt is a synchronous machine instruction executed within the program that causes a transfer of control through the interrupt mechanism, typically used for low-level system calls to the OS or device drivers
questions.explanationEn: Slide 23 explains that a software interrupt is actually a machine instruction that causes a transfer of control through the same mechanism used by true interrupts, typically used for low-level calls to the operating system or device drivers.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 23 giải thích rằng ngắt mềm (Software interrupt) thực chất là một lệnh máy chủ động chuyển quyền điều khiển qua cơ chế giống như ngắt thật, thường dùng để gọi hàm hệ thống mức thấp tới Hệ điều hành (OS) hoặc trình điều khiển thiết bị (device drivers).

questions.subtopic: Polling vs. Interrupt-Driven I/O Utilization
questions.concept: Processing without interrupts vs. with interrupts (Figure 3.7)
questions.question: In Figure 3.7 (Program Flow of Control without and with Interrupts, Slides 25–27), how does 'Processing with interrupts (short I/O wait)' improve CPU utilization during a WRITE operation compared to 'Processing without interrupts'?
options: The CPU increases the printer's mechanical paper speed by 1,000 times
The user program skips all I/O commands and discards the output data
The I/O device executes user arithmetic instructions while the CPU powers down

After the OS prepares the I/O transfer and issues the I/O command (Block 4), control returns immediately to the user program so the CPU executes the next user code segment concurrently while the slow I/O device operates
questions.explanationEn: Slides 26–27 show that without interrupts, the user's program is suspended while the OS waits and polls the device status until I/O completes. With interrupts, after write preparation in Block 4, control returns to the user program so I/O proceeds concurrently with user program execution until the device issues an interrupt request.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 26–27: Không có ngắt, chương trình người dùng bị treo để đợi và hỏi vòng (poll) trạng thái thiết bị cho đến khi I/O xong. Có ngắt, sau khi chuẩn bị và phát lệnh I/O ở khối 4, CPU quay lại thực thi chương trình người dùng song song với quá trình hoạt động của thiết bị I/O.

questions.subtopic: Interrupt Cycle & State Diagram with Interrupts
questions.concept: Processor actions during the Interrupt Cycle
questions.question: When an interrupt signal is pending at the start of the Interrupt Cycle, what exact actions does the processor perform before branching to the interrupt handler routine?
options: It suspends execution of the current program, saves the context (including the address of the next instruction to be executed and relevant processor status), and sets the Program Counter (PC) to the starting address of the interrupt handler
It permanently deletes the current user process from main memory and reboots the operating system
It halts the system clock until the user presses a key on the keyboard
It copies the entire hard disk into the Instruction Register (IR)
questions.explanationEn: Slides 29 and 31 specify that when an interrupt is pending, the processor suspends execution of the current program, saves context (the address of the next instruction to be executed and other relevant data), and sets the PC to the starting address of the interrupt handler routine.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 29 và 31: Khi có ngắt đang chờ, bộ xử lý tạm dừng chương trình hiện tại, lưu ngữ cảnh (địa chỉ lệnh kế tiếp và trạng thái hiện hành của CPU), rồi gán PC bằng địa chỉ bắt đầu của trình phục vụ ngắt (interrupt handler).

questions.subtopic: Multiple Interrupts (Disable vs. Priority) & x86 IVT
questions.concept: Two strategies for handling multiple interrupts
questions.question: What are the two fundamental strategies for handling multiple overlapping interrupts described on Slide 36?
options: (1) Ignore all I/O interrupts permanently; and (2) Reboot the CPU whenever two interrupts arrive together
(1) Convert hardware interrupts into syntax errors; and (2) Store interrupts on magnetic tape

(1) Disable interrupts while processing an interrupt (handling pending interrupts sequentially after the current one finishes); and (2) Define priorities so a higher-priority interrupt can preempt a lower-priority interrupt handler
(1) Use big-endian byte ordering; and (2) Use direct cache mapping
questions.explanationEn: Slide 36 outlines the two strategies for handling multiple interrupts: (1) Disable interrupts (processor ignores further interrupts while processing one; pending interrupts are checked and handled in sequence afterward), and (2) Define priorities (low-priority interrupts can be interrupted by higher-priority interrupts, returning to the previous interrupt when finished).
questions.explanationVi: Slide 36 trình bày 2 chiến lược xử lý đa ngắt: (1) Cấm ngắt (Disable interrupts) trong khi đang xử lý một ngắt để phục vụ tuần tự; (2) Phân mức ưu tiên (Define priorities) cho phép ngắt có độ ưu tiên cao hơn tạm dừng ngắt có độ ưu tiên thấp hơn.

questions.subtopic: Multiple Interrupts (Disable vs. Priority) & x86 IVT
questions.concept: x86 Interrupt Vector Table (IVT) Size and Entry Address Calculation
questions.question: In the x86 real-mode Interrupt Vector Table (IVT) located at memory address `0x0000:0000` (Slide 39), there are 256 interrupt vectors (`0` to `255`), and each entry stores a 4-byte `segment:offset` pointer. What is the total size of the IVT, and at what hexadecimal byte address in the table is the ISR pointer for `INT 21h` (decimal 33) stored?
options: Total IVT size = 256 bytes; ISR pointer for INT 21h is at address 0x0021 (decimal 33)
Total IVT size = 4096 bytes (4 KB); ISR pointer for INT 21h is at address 0x0210
Total IVT size = 512 bytes; ISR pointer for INT 21h is at address 0x0042 (decimal 66)
Total IVT size = 1024 bytes (1 KB); ISR pointer for INT 21h is at address 0x0084 (decimal 132)
questions.explanationEn: From Slide 39: Total IVT size = 256 entries × 4 bytes/entry = 1024 bytes = 1 KB. For `INT n`, the ISR vector is stored at address `n × 4`. For `n = 21h = 33` decimal: `33 × 4 = 132` decimal = `0x0084` (or in hex: `0x21 × 4 = 0x84`).
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 39: Bảng vector ngắt (IVT) gồm 256 mục × 4 byte = 1024 bytes = 1 KB. Địa chỉ lưu con trỏ ISR của lệnh `INT n` là `n × 4`. Với `n = 21h = 33`: địa chỉ là `33 × 4 = 132` (thập phân) = `0x0084` (thập lục phân).
questions.stepByStep:
1. Compute total table size: 256 vectors × 4 bytes = 1024 bytes = 1 KB.
2. Convert vector number n = 21h to decimal: 2 × 16 + 1 = 33.
3. Multiply by 4 bytes per entry: 33 × 4 = 132 = 0x0084.

questions.subtopic: Direct Memory Access (DMA)
questions.concept: Direct Memory Access (DMA) principle
questions.question: How does Direct Memory Access (DMA) improve system efficiency during large I/O data transfers?
options: The processor executes a tight polling loop to copy every single byte through the Accumulator register
The I/O device writes data directly into the CPU's Program Counter
DMA eliminates main memory by storing all files inside the ALU
The processor grants permission to the DMA/I/O module to exchange data directly with main memory over the bus, allowing the processor to proceed with other work
questions.explanationEn: Slide 44 (p. 16) explains that in Direct Memory Access (DMA), the processor grants permission for I/O devices to exchange data directly with memory, and the processor can then proceed to other work (provided it does not need the bus granted to the DMA module).
questions.explanationVi: Slide 44 (trang 16) giải thích: Với cơ chế Truy cập bộ nhớ trực tiếp (DMA), CPU cấp quyền cho mô-đun I/O trao đổi dữ liệu trực tiếp với bộ nhớ chính, giúp CPU rảnh tay thực hiện các công việc khác.

questions.subtopic: I/O Modules, Ports & Peripheral Data Traffic
questions.concept: Comparing peripheral data traffic rates and control types
questions.question: According to the I/O systems table on Slide 47, which peripheral has the highest data traffic rate (ca. 500 MB/s), and how are Ethernet network interfaces and Hard Disks (HDD) classified in terms of control and direction?
options: Keyboard has the highest data traffic (ca. 500 MB/s); Graphics card is Input-only
Modem has the highest data traffic (ca. 50 MB/s); GPS is Output-only
Printer has a higher data traffic rate (ca. 200 kB/s) than a Hard Disk Drive (ca. 50 MB/s)
Graphics card has the highest data traffic (ca. 500 MB/s, Human-controlled, Output); Ethernet (ca. 12.5 MB/s) and Disk/HDD (ca. 50 MB/s) are Machine-controlled with In/Out direction
questions.explanationEn: Slide 47 lists peripheral traffic rates: Keyboard (100 byte/s, Human, Input), Mouse (200 byte/s, Human, Input), Sound (96 kB/s, Output), Printer (200 kB/s, Output), Graphics card (500 MB/s, Human, Output), Modem (2–8 kB/s, Machine, In/Out), Ethernet (12.5 MB/s, Machine, In/Out), Disk HDD (50 MB/s, Machine, In/Out), GPS (100 byte/s, Machine, Input).
questions.explanationVi: Theo bảng Slide 47 (trang 17): Card đồ họa (Graphics card) có lưu lượng cao nhất (~500 MB/s, Output). Cạc mạng Ethernet (~12.5 MB/s) và Ổ cứng HDD (~50 MB/s) đều do Máy điều khiển (Machine) và truyền hai chiều (In/Out).

questions.subtopic: Separate (Isolated) I/O vs. Memory-Mapped I/O
questions.concept: Separate (Isolated) I/O vs. Memory-Mapped I/O
questions.question: How does 'Memory-Mapped I/O' (Slide 51) differ from the 'Separate (Isolated) Memory and I/O Address Space' used in x86 (Slides 49–50)?
options: In Memory-Mapped I/O, I/O devices cannot be accessed by the CPU at all
In Separate I/O, no address bus is used and all devices share a single register

In Memory-Mapped I/O, the CPU has a single unified address space with special addresses reserved for I/O devices and uses standard memory read/write instructions; in Separate I/O, memory (e.g., 4 GB) and I/O (e.g., 64 KB) have separate address spaces and use distinct instructions or a MEM/IO# selector signal
Memory-Mapped I/O requires two separate CPUs, one for RAM and one for I/O
questions.explanationEn: Slides 49–51 contrast Separate I/O (two separate address spaces, such as x86's 4 GB memory space and 64 KB I/O space, using separate I/O instructions like `R0 <- IO[0x60]` or a shared bus with a `MEM/IO#` selector line) with Memory-Mapped I/O (a single address space where reserved addresses are answered by I/O devices using standard memory requests).
questions.explanationVi: Slide 49–51 phân biệt: Vào/ra tách biệt (Separate I/O, như trên x86 có 4GB bộ nhớ và 64KB I/O riêng) dùng lệnh I/O riêng hoặc tín hiệu chọn `MEM/IO#`; trong khi Vào/ra ánh xạ bộ nhớ (Memory-mapped I/O) dùng chung một không gian địa chỉ duy nhất cho cả bộ nhớ và thiết bị I/O.

questions.subtopic: Five Types of Data Transfers
questions.concept: Five types of transfers supported by the interconnection structure
questions.question: What are the five types of data transfers that a computer's interconnection structure must support (Slide 58)?
options: Compiler to assembler, Assembler to linker, Linker to loader, Loader to OS, and OS to user
L1 to L2, L2 to L3, L3 to RAM, RAM to SSD, and SSD to Cloud
Fetch, Decode, Execute, Interrupt, and Halt
Memory to processor, Processor to memory, I/O to processor, Processor to I/O, and I/O to or from memory (using DMA)
questions.explanationEn: Slide 58 lists the five required transfer types: (1) Memory to processor, (2) Processor to memory, (3) I/O to processor, (4) Processor to I/O, and (5) I/O to or from memory (direct memory access).
questions.explanationVi: Slide 58 liệt kê 5 kiểu truyền dữ liệu mà cấu trúc kết nối phải hỗ trợ: (1) Bộ nhớ -> CPU, (2) CPU -> Bộ nhớ, (3) I/O -> CPU, (4) CPU -> I/O, và (5) I/O <-> Bộ nhớ trực tiếp qua DMA.

questions.subtopic: Data, Address & Control Bus Lines (MRDC, MWRC, IORC, IOWC)
questions.concept: Control Bus Signals and Active-Low Commands
questions.question: Which of the following groups lists typical Control Bus signals (Slides 71 & 85), including the four standard active-low read/write command lines?
options: RAX, RBX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, RBP, and RSP
Tag bits, Set index bits, Block offset bits, and LRU counter
SISD, SIMD, MIMD, and MISD
Memory Read Control (MRDC), Memory Write Control (MWRC), I/O Read Control (IORC), I/O Write Control (IOWC), Transfer ACK, Bus Request/Grant, Interrupt Request/ACK, Clock, and Reset
questions.explanationEn: Slide 71 lists typical control signals (Memory read/write, I/O read/write, Bus request/grant, Transfer ACK, Interrupt Request/ACK, Clock, Reset), and Slide 85 names the four standard active-low control bus connections: MRDC (Memory Read Control), MWRC (Memory Write Control), IORC (I/O Read Control), and IOWC (I/O Write Control).
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 71 và 85, các tín hiệu trên Bus điều khiển gồm: MRDC (Đọc bộ nhớ), MWRC (Ghi bộ nhớ), IORC (Đọc I/O), IOWC (Ghi I/O), Transfer ACK, Bus request/grant, Interrupt request/ACK, Clock và Reset.

questions.subtopic: Bus Types, Arbitration, Timing & Bus Width Calculations
questions.concept: Dedicated vs. Multiplexed Buses and Centralized vs. Distributed Arbitration
questions.question: What is the primary trade-off between a Dedicated bus and a Time-Multiplexed bus (Slide 77), and what is the difference between a 'Master' and a 'Slave' device in bus arbitration (Slide 78)?
options: A multiplexed bus uses twice as many wires as a dedicated bus; the Slave initiates the transfer while the Master waits
A dedicated bus cannot transfer data in parallel; Master and Slave refer to hard disk platters

A multiplexed bus uses fewer physical lines by sharing lines for address and data (using an Address Valid or Data Valid control line) at the cost of more complex control and lower performance; the Master initiates the data transfer on the bus while the Slave is the target device involved in the exchange
Time-multiplexed buses do not require any control lines; only I/O devices can act as bus Masters
questions.explanationEn: Slide 77 explains that time-multiplexed buses share lines using an Address Valid or Data Valid control signal—saving wires, but requiring more complex control and reducing performance because address and data cannot appear simultaneously. Slide 78 defines the device that initiates data transfer as the Master and the other device involved as the Slave.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 77–78 giải thích: Bus dồn kênh (Multiplexed bus) dùng chung đường truyền cho địa chỉ và dữ liệu giúp giảm số dây dẫn nhưng điều khiển phức tạp hơn và giảm hiệu năng. Thiết bị khởi tạo truyền dữ liệu gọi là Master (chủ), thiết bị phản hồi gọi là Slave (tớ).

questions.subtopic: Bus Types, Arbitration, Timing & Bus Width Calculations
questions.concept: Synchronous vs. Asynchronous Bus Timing
questions.question: How does Asynchronous Bus Timing differ from Synchronous Bus Timing (Slides 79–81)?
options: In Asynchronous timing, all devices are locked to a fixed high-frequency clock crystal
Synchronous timing cannot be tested and requires no clock line on the control bus
Asynchronous timing is simpler to implement than synchronous timing but only supports a single device speed

questions.concept: Nested Priority Interrupts Execution Order
questions.question: Suppose a system uses Priority-Based Multiple Interrupt handling (Strategy 2 on Slide 36) where Printer has priority 2, Communication Line has priority 5, and Disk has priority 4 (higher number = higher priority). While the User Program is running, a Printer interrupt occurs at t=10. While the Printer ISR is running, a Communication interrupt arrives at t=15, and while the Communication ISR is running, a Disk interrupt arrives at t=20. In what order do the ISRs complete?
options: Printer ISR completes first, then Communication ISR, then Disk ISR
Disk ISR preempts Communication ISR and completes first
All three interrupts are discarded and the User Program continues
Communication ISR (priority 5) completes first, then Disk ISR (priority 4) runs and completes, and finally Printer ISR (priority 2) resumes and completes before returning to the User Program
questions.explanationEn: Under priority interrupt handling: Printer (prio 2) interrupts User Program at t=10. At t=15, Communication (prio 5 > 2) preempts Printer ISR. At t=20, Disk (prio 4 < 5) arrives but is lower priority than Communication, so it remains pending until Communication ISR finishes. Once Communication ISR finishes, Disk ISR (prio 4 > 2) runs and completes, and finally Printer ISR (prio 2) finishes.
questions.explanationVi: Theo cơ chế ngắt ưu tiên: Ngắt Máy in (mức 2) đang chạy thì bị Ngắt Truyền thông (mức 5 > 2) chiếm quyền tại t=15. Tại t=20, Ngắt Đĩa từ (mức 4 < 5) đến nhưng thấp hơn mức 5 nên phải chờ. Sau khi Truyền thông (mức 5) xong, Đĩa từ (mức 4 > 2) được thực thi xong, rồi mới quay lại hoàn tất Máy in (mức 2).

options: Attaching many devices to a single bus causes long data paths (propagation delays) and severe bottlenecks when aggregate data transfer approaches bus capacity; hierarchical buses isolate high-speed devices (graphics, video, LAN, SCSI) from slower serial/modem expansion devices
A single bus can only support 2 bits of data width

Kiến trúc đa bus phân cấp tách các thiết bị tốc độ cao (đồ họa, video, mạng LAN, SCSI) lên High-speed bus và các thiết bị chậm (modem, serial, fax) xuống Expansion bus.

questions.subtopic: Bus Types, Arbitration, Timing & Bus Width Calculations
questions.concept: Calculating Data Bus Bandwidth from Width and Frequency
questions.question: A synchronous system bus has a Data Bus width of 64 bits and operates at a bus clock frequency of 100 MHz, transferring one 64-bit word per bus cycle. What is the maximum theoretical data transfer rate (bandwidth) in Megabytes per second (MB/s, where 1 MB = 10^6 bytes for transfer rate)?
options: 100 MB/s
64 MB/s
800 MB/s (8 bytes/cycle × 100 × 10^6 cycles/s)
questions.explanationEn: A 64-bit data bus transfers 64 / 8 = 8 bytes per bus cycle. At 100 MHz (100 × 10^6 cycles/second), the transfer rate is 8 bytes/cycle × 100 × 10^6 cycles/s = 800 × 10^6 bytes/s = 800 MB/s.
questions.explanationVi: Bus dữ liệu 64-bit truyền được 64 / 8 = 8 bytes mỗi chu kỳ. Ở tần số 100 MHz (100 triệu chu kỳ/giây), tốc độ truyền tối đa là 8 × 100 = 800 MB/s.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Convert data bus width to bytes: 64 bits / 8 bits/byte = 8 bytes per transfer.
2. Multiply by clock rate (100 × 10^6 cycles/s): 8 × 100 × 10^6 = 800 × 10^6 B/s = 800 MB/s.

questions.subtopic: Separate (Isolated) I/O vs. Memory-Mapped I/O
questions.concept: x86 I/O Address Space Port Count from 0000H to FFFFH
questions.question: Slide 84 states that for an x86 I/O operation, an address value between `0000H` and `FFFFH` is issued on the address lines (corresponding to the `0 – 64 KB` I/O address space on Slide 49). How many bits of the address bus are used to specify this I/O address range, and how many distinct 8-bit I/O ports can be addressed?
options: 20 address bits; 1,048,576 (2^20) I/O ports
16 address bits; 65,536 (2^16) distinct 8-bit I/O ports
8 address bits; 256 (2^8) I/O ports
32 address bits; 4,294,967,296 I/O ports
questions.explanationEn: A 4-digit hexadecimal address from `0000H` to `FFFFH` uses 4 × 4 = 16 bits, giving 2^16 = 65,536 (64K) distinct byte-addressable I/O port addresses.
questions.explanationVi: Dải địa chỉ I/O từ `0000H` đến `FFFFH` (Slide 84) gồm 4 chữ số hex tương ứng với 16 bit địa chỉ, cho phép định địa chỉ 2^16 = 65,536 (64K) cổng I/O 8-bit.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Hex range 0000H to FFFFH requires 4 hex digits × 4 bits/digit = 16 bits.
2. Total distinct addresses = 2^16 = 65,536 (64K ports).
